pairs.subject: test-input-generation
pairs.evidence: src/features/shared/components/forms/NumberStepper.tsx:192 NumberStepper's typed-text parser has a rejection branch for non-numeric input (it reverts the draft to the last committed value), but its only test file feeds the parser just '999' (numeric, out of range) and '' (empty), so this branch is never exercised and the suite still passes.

techniques.evidence: src/features/shared/components/forms/NumberStepper.tsx:192 NumberStepper.test.tsx is the only test file that names NumberStepper. It tests the accept path and clamping ('999' at test line 93, '' at line 87), but never a non-numeric draft like 'abc', and never near-boundary inputs Number() accepts unexpectedly ('1e3', '0x10', 'Infinity'). The rejection surface is untested. The parseHex tests in ColorPicker.test.tsx do include near-boundary rejects ('fff', '#ggg'), so the colour parser does better here.

pairs.registryProposal: Most of this subject's techniques assume a randomized or fuzz generator already exists. Small UI-component suites built only from hand-picked examples have no technique saying when a single example that stands in for a general property (e.g. 'no float drift' from one case) should become an enumerated or generated input set. Adding a use_when for example-only suites would let such contexts be judged instead of left unread.
